werk/vandenberg-burning-heart.text: In 1982, Burning Heart was released by the band of guitarist Adrian Vandenberg. It is a power ballad: a quiet beginning, a big chorus and a guitar solo that builds to a climax. It became a hit in the United States. Vandenberg made hard rock that sounded exactly the way American rock radio wanted it. Later he became guitarist of the British band Whitesnake. There was nothing Dutch to be heard in Burning Heart, and that was the intention.
werk/vandenberg-burning-heart.listen: Listen for the build-up of the power ballad: a quiet beginning, a big chorus and a guitar solo that lifts the song.

werk/vangelis-albedo-0-39.text:
Albedo 0.39 was released in 1976 and was the second album that Vangelis recorded in his Nemo Studios in London, his workplace until the end of the 1980s. It contrasts with its predecessor Heaven and Hell, which had a classical tinge and used choirs. Albedo 0.39, by contrast, has blues and jazz colours. It is a concept album about space physics, named after the fraction of light that a planet reflects: for the Earth this was calculated in 1976 at 0.39.

Vangelis plays everything himself, from synthesizers to drums, xylophone and gamelan. Pulstar builds on a pulsating synthesizer sequence and ends with a recording of the speaking clock. Mare Tranquillitatis uses recordings of Apollo moon landings. On the title song, sound engineer Keith Spencer-Allen reads out properties of the Earth. The album reached number 18 on the British album chart, his first record in the top twenty.
werk/vangelis-albedo-0-39.listen: Listen to Pulstar and notice the pulsating synthesizer sequence on which the piece is built, and the recording of the speaking clock at the end.

werk/vangelis-china.text:
China was released in April 1979. At the end of 1978, Vangelis no longer had a record contract, and he found a home at Polydor. He had never been to China himself, but he had been fascinated by the country for years. He did not want to make Chinese folk music, but to capture China as he felt it. It is a loose concept album with tracks that refer to the Long March, the dragon, yin and yang and the Himalayas. He played synthesizers, piano and Chinese flutes and plucked string instruments, in a studio with new 24-track equipment.

The music does not sound like real world music, but like ordered, simple melodies with a Chinese colouring. Chung Kuo begins with steam locomotive sounds and percussion, The Long March is a piano solo, and Himalaya conjures up a cold, windswept mountain landscape with broad washes of sound. AllMusic felt that Vangelis succeeded well in evoking the majesty of China.
werk/vangelis-china.listen: Listen to Himalaya and notice how the long washes of sound evoke a cold, windswept mountain landscape: which sounds create that feeling?

werk/vangelis-l-apocalypse-des-animaux.text:
L’Apocalypse des animaux is a soundtrack album for a documentary series about the animal kingdom by the French director Frédéric Rossif, which was shown on French television in 1973. The music was recorded as early as 1970, when Vangelis was still a member of the progressive rock band Aphrodite's Child. It was his first collaboration with Rossif.

The working method is remarkable. Vangelis was not shown the footage. He recorded a series of separate pieces around the theme of nature and let the filmmakers choose from them what they needed. Later he would compose while watching the film. In the documentary far more music is heard than appears on the album, as is often the case with his soundtracks. The record reflects a period in which he was very productive and liked to experiment with technology and styles.
werk/vangelis-l-apocalypse-des-animaux.listen: Listen to Création du monde, at more than ten minutes the longest piece, and follow how the music unfolds as a free-floating soundscape, with no fixed images to lean on.

werk/vangelis-spiral.text:
Spiral was released in December 1977. It was the third album that Vangelis recorded in his Nemo Studios in London, where he worked until the end of the 1980s. He produced and arranged it himself, played all the instruments and also designed the sleeve. The record came after Heaven and Hell and Albedo 0.39 and became less well known and less praised than those two.

It is a concept album, inspired by ancient Taoist philosophy and the idea that the universe moves in spirals. The album is almost entirely instrumental and uses synthesizers, sequencers, electric piano and percussion. For the first time on a Vangelis album the Yamaha CS-80 is heard, a synthesizer to which he often returned later. Dervish D is intended as music for a whirling dervish. For To the Unknown Man he received the Midem International Instrumental award in 1978.
werk/vangelis-spiral.listen: Listen to Dervish D and notice how the music keeps turning: do you hear a repetition that moves a little further each time?

werk/wadada-leo-smith-golden-quartet.text:
Golden Quartet was recorded in 2000 and released on Tzadik Records. It was the first record by the quartet of that name, led by trumpeter and flugelhorn player Wadada Leo Smith. Anthony Davis plays piano, Malachi Favors bass and Jack DeJohnette drums. The album contains five pieces, often dedicated to someone: DeJohnette to the drummer, Harumi to Harumi Makino Smith, and Celestial Sky and All the Magic is a memorial piece for Lester Bowie.

AllMusic called it his strongest record as a bandleader in a long time and his best for Tzadik. The Penguin Guide to Jazz wrote that in Celestial Sky and All the Magic he again shows how much he owes to Miles Davis, but also how far beyond him he has since come.
werk/wadada-leo-smith-golden-quartet.listen: In Celestial Sky and All the Magic, listen to the trumpet and notice what you recognise of Miles Davis.

werk/wadada-leo-smith-kulture-jazz.text:
Kulture Jazz is a solo album by the American trumpeter and composer Wadada Leo Smith. He recorded it in October 1992, and it was released a year later on ECM. It was his second record for that label, after Divine Love from 1979. Smith stands completely alone in the studio. He plays trumpet, flugelhorn, koto, mbira, harmonica, a bamboo notched flute and percussion, and he also sings himself.

The reception was glowing. AllMusic reviewer Eugene Chadbourne felt that ECM does Smith better justice here than ever, and he praised how the record presents folk, blues, jazz and creative music as related forms. A reviewer for Jazz Desk compared the album to someone building his own house or boat or sewing his own clothes. The music is very personal and at times has an almost meditative quality.
werk/wadada-leo-smith-kulture-jazz.listen: Listen to Kulture of Jazz and bear in mind that everything you hear is played by one musician. Notice the moments that feel almost meditative.

werk/wadada-leo-smith-light-upon-light.text:
Light Upon Light was released in 1999 in the Composer Series of Tzadik Records. It is the second album that trumpeter Wadada Leo Smith recorded for that label. It contains five pieces in widely differing forms: a composition for chamber ensemble and gamelan quartet, a solo piece for viola, a double bass concerto that he wrote for Bert Turetzky and two electronic pieces. In the first piece, Moths, Flames and the Giant Sequoia Redwood Trees, gamelan instruments such as gender, kempul and gong ageng are heard, and he plays kenong himself. In Multiamerica and A Thousand Cranes, a memorial piece for Amir Hamzehi, he plays trumpet with electronics by Mark Trayle.

AllMusic wrote that the album is more spacious and a little colder than his first for Tzadik, Tao-Njia.
werk/wadada-leo-smith-light-upon-light.listen: In Multiamerica, listen to how the trumpet combines with electronics and spoken poetry.

werk/wanda-jackson-right-or-wrong.text:
Right or Wrong was recorded on 28 October 1960 at the Bradley studio in Nashville and released in October 1961 on Capitol Records. Wanda Jackson, a country and rockabilly singer, sang the lead vocals and played guitar. Among the accompanists were Buck Owens, Roy Clark and Marvin Hughes. The sleeve promises six sugar-coated ballads and six songs with a big beat. Country songs thus sit alongside rockers, including Stupid Cupid and Brown Eyed Handsome Man by Chuck Berry.

The title song, written by Jackson herself, reached number 9 on the country chart and number 29 on the pop chart. Later CD editions include bonus tracks such as You Can't Have My Love and Let's Have a Party. AllMusic gave one of those reissues two and a half stars.
werk/wanda-jackson-right-or-wrong.listen: Listen to Right or Wrong, the song that Jackson wrote herself and that became the hit of the record, and notice her voice.

werk/wanda-jackson-there-s-a-party-goin-.text:
There's a Party Goin' On was released in January 1961 on Capitol Records. The sleeve describes it as a collection of good country songs in the rhythmic singing style of Wanda Jackson, who sang both country and rockabilly. The album contains twelve songs by well-known writers: the title song by Don Covay and John Berry, Kansas City by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, Lonely Week-Ends by Charlie Rich, It Doesn't Matter Anymore by Paul Anka and Fallin' by Neil Sedaka and Howard Greenfield.

AllMusic gave the album four stars. Reviewer Richie Unterberger called it a solid, energetic set, with lightning-fast rockabilly guitar work by Roy Clark. Most of the songs last only two to three minutes.
werk/wanda-jackson-there-s-a-party-goin-.listen: In There's a Party Goin' On, listen to the tempo: the song barely lasts two minutes.

werk/wayne-shorter-speak-no-evil.text:
Speak No Evil is Wayne Shorter's sixth album, released in June 1966 on Blue Note. He recorded it in 1964, his first year in Miles Davis's quintet, alongside several other records for Blue Note. The music combines hard bop and modal jazz. Alongside Shorter on tenor saxophone play trumpeter Freddie Hubbard, pianist Herbie Hancock, bassist Ron Carter and drummer Elvin Jones. All the pieces are by Shorter himself.

The album is regarded as one of his best and as a high point of the Blue Note catalogue. The Penguin Guide to Jazz called it his most satisfying record. Murray Horwitz said in 2001 that it was almost a manifesto for his ideas, which had been new forty years earlier and still sounded fresh. Ben Ratliff wrote that almost every jazz musician born in or after the 1950s accepts this work as a foundation.
werk/wayne-shorter-speak-no-evil.listen: Listen to Infant Eyes. This is the only piece in which Freddie Hubbard does not play: notice how that changes the sound of the group.

werk/wayne-shorter-wayning-moments.text:
Wayning Moments is saxophonist Wayne Shorter's third album and his last for Vee-Jay Records. It is a hard bop record that was recorded in November 1961, on the second and the sixth of that month. Alongside the bandleader on tenor saxophone play trumpeter Freddie Hubbard, pianist Eddie Higgins, bassist Jymie Merritt and drummer Marshall Thompson.

The repertoire is mixed. The saxophonist himself wrote Devil's Island, Dead End, Powder Keg and Callaway Went That-A-Way. Black Orpheus is by Luiz Bonfá and Antônio Maria, Moon of Manakoora by Frank Loesser and Alfred Newman, and All or Nothing at All by Arthur Altman and Jack Lawrence. The title song is by pianist Higgins. Later CD editions added alternate takes of all eight tracks, so that you can hear how the band played the same pieces each time in a slightly different way.
werk/wayne-shorter-wayning-moments.listen: Listen to Black Orpheus and notice how saxophone and trumpet share the melody. Can you hear which of the two takes a solo first?

werk/weather-report-heavy-weather.text:
Weather Report's seventh album was released in 1977 on Columbia. The founders Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter played together with bassist Jaco Pastorius, drummer Alex Acuña and percussionist Manolo Badrena. Zawinul produced and orchestrated, Shorter and Pastorius did additional production. The record opens with Birdland, an instrumental piece that nevertheless became a great success and later a jazz standard.

Teen Town, a composition by Pastorius in which his bass plays the leading role, is regarded as a highlight of the record. Rumba Mamá, with Badrena and Acuña in the foreground, was recorded live at the concert in Montreux in the summer of 1976. Rolling Stone felt that the group had lost space and lightness, but that the new bassist made their music busier and more talkative. The record became the group's most commercially successful album and in 2011 was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/weather-report-heavy-weather.listen: Listen to Teen Town and notice Pastorius's bass, which plays the leading role here.

werk/weather-report-i-sing-the-body-elec.text:
I Sing the Body Electric is Weather Report's second studio album, from 1972. The band gained two new members: percussionist Dom Um Romão and drummer Eric Gravatt. The title comes from a poem by Walt Whitman from 1855 and from a short story by Ray Bradbury from 1969. The last three tracks were recorded live in Tokyo on 13 January 1972 and edited for this album. The whole concert was released separately as an import record under the title Live in Tokyo.

According to AllMusic, the studio tracks are more biting, more ethnically varied and more loaded with electronic effects and grand structures than before. The live pieces are fiercer still and for the first time reveal the group's enormous drive. Robert Christgau found the record neater and more sterile than the debut and less Miles Davis-sounding, and he was interested in it, but not gripped.
werk/weather-report-i-sing-the-body-elec.listen: Listen to Directions, one of the live tracks recorded in Tokyo, and notice the band's drive in comparison with the studio tracks at the beginning of the record.

werk/weather-report-mysterious-traveller.text:
For Weather Report's fourth album, founder Miroslav Vitouš left because of creative differences. Alphonso Johnson came in on bass, and Ishmael Wilburn became the new drummer. The album was released in 1974.

It is the first record by the group to use mainly electric bass, with funk, R&B grooves and rock that later became the trademark. The composition became tighter, in place of the open improvisation of the first three albums. The readers of DownBeat chose it as album of the year for 1974, and the magazine gave it five stars. The Penguin Guide included it in its core collection of essential recordings. On the Billboard Jazz Albums chart it reached number 2.
werk/weather-report-mysterious-traveller.listen: Listen to Mysterious Traveller and notice the electric bass and the funk-like groove beneath the melody.

werk/weather-report-sweetnighter.text:
Weather Report recorded Sweetnighter in February 1973 in less than a week at a studio in Connecticut. Josef Zawinul increasingly took the lead and steered the group away from the collective improvisation of their concerts towards more clearly structured pieces with funk and groove. Bassist Miroslav Vitouš played on it for the last time as principal bassist, and the electric bass now sounds much more prominent.

For that reason the album is regarded as the transition between the open style of the first records and the tighter, composed music. The two long pieces Boogie Woogie Waltz and 125th Street Congress are the core, with Non-Stop Home as the closer. Robert Christgau found Boogie Woogie Waltz fatally cute, despite the good improvisations. The piece remained a frequent live number in the 1970s.
werk/weather-report-sweetnighter.listen: Listen to 125th Street Congress and notice how the rhythm carries the groove here.

werk/weezer-hurley.text:
Hurley is Weezer's eighth album and was released on 10 September 2010. It was the first and only record on the independent label Epitaph. At the end of 2009 the group had lost its contract with Geffen, after the previous record, Raditude, had been received lukewarmly. Rivers Cuomo and Shawn Everett produced the album, which, like the one before, contains songs written with outside writers.

Cuomo promised more raw rock energy. The opener Memories, with members of Jackass on backing vocals, became the first single. In Hang On, co-written by Rick Nowels, the actor Michael Cera plays mandolin and sings along. The closer Time Flies has a lo-fi folk and country sound. The cover shows the actor Jorge Garcia, who played Hurley in the series Lost. Critics received the record mostly favourably. Some called it the group's strongest record in years.
werk/weezer-hurley.listen: Listen to Memories and notice the raw energy and the strings in this opening track.

werk/weezer-make-believe.text:
Make Believe took almost three years. During the recording the band put dozens of demos online, but eventually decided to start completely afresh, with producer Rick Rubin. Rivers Cuomo discovered meditation in that period, which influenced his lyrics. Pardon Me came about after a ten-day course, and Haunt You Every Day was the first song he wrote entirely on piano, at Rubin's request. Personal lyrics returned after two records on which he had kept more distance.

Beverly Hills was the big hit and brought the group their first Grammy nomination. The album entered at number two on the Billboard 200. The reviews varied widely. AllMusic and Rolling Stone were positive and compared it with Pinkerton, while Pitchfork rated it 0.4. Even so, the album kept selling steadily. According to Cuomo, the title came to him while meditating.
werk/weezer-make-believe.listen: Listen to Haunt You Every Day and notice the piano as the central instrument, which makes this song sound different from typical Weezer.

werk/weezer-maladroit.text:
For their fourth album, the members of Weezer took a new path: during the recording they put demos on their website as MP3s every day to get reactions from fans. As a result, dozens of versions of more than thirty songs were circulating before the record came out. Radio stations even played the unfinished songs, which led to a dispute with the record company Geffen, because the band had paid for the sessions themselves. It was the first album with bassist Scott Shriner, and the group produced it themselves.

The sound is harder than before, with riffs that seem to come from heavy metal. Dope Nose and Keep Fishin' were the singles, and at fans' request Slob returned. The title, which means maladroit, was thought up by someone on the band's forum. The reviews were mostly good, although IGN found it a mixed result. Later writers called the album underrated.
werk/weezer-maladroit.listen: Listen to Dope Nose and notice the heavy, driving guitars beneath a very accessible melody.

werk/weezer-pinkerton.text:
After the great success of the 1994 debut, Rivers Cuomo felt constrained by rock music. He dropped the plan for a rock opera and wrote most of the second album during his studies at Harvard. The band recorded the songs in 1995 and 1996 at Electric Lady Studios in New York and Sound City Studios in Los Angeles, without a producer, to get closer to Weezer's live sound.

The result sounds darker and rawer than the debut: screeching guitars, hard rhythms and vocals right at the front of the mix. The lyrics deal with loneliness, sexual frustration and doubt about the rock life. Tired of Sex opens, El Scorcho is about Cuomo's shyness towards a woman, and The Good Life about his isolation at Harvard. The title comes from a character in Puccini's Madama Butterfly. The reviews were mixed and sales disappointed, but appreciation grew later and several emo bands named the album as an influence.
werk/weezer-pinkerton.listen: Listen to Across the Sea and notice how far forward the vocals sit in the mix, in a song about a Japanese fan whom Cuomo will never meet.

werk/weezer-raditude.text:
Raditude is Weezer's seventh album and was released on 3 November 2009. It was the last on DGC and Interscope. The title was thought up by the actor Rainn Wilson, and the cover shows a dog. Rivers Cuomo sings all the lead vocals, and drummer Josh Freese played because Patrick Wilson took over Cuomo's guitar. Jacknife Lee was the producer.

The sound is mainstream pop, with help from outside writers. Cuomo wrote Can't Stop Partying together with Jermaine Dupri, with Lil Wayne as guest rapper. The first single was (If You're Wondering If I Want You To) I Want You To. In I'm Your Daddy, Kenny G plays a solo. The reception was mixed. AllMusic found the album full of creative energy; other critics called the lyrics juvenile. Guitarist Brian Bell himself had doubts about the pop direction.
werk/weezer-raditude.listen: Listen to I'm Your Daddy and notice Kenny G's solo after the second chorus, which he recorded in a single take.

werk/wes-montgomery-movin-along.text:
Movin' Along is an album by the American jazz guitarist Wes Montgomery and was released in April 1961 on Riverside. The producer was Orrin Keepnews. Alongside Montgomery play James Clay on flute and tenor saxophone, pianist Victor Feldman, bassist Sam Jones and drummer Louis Hayes. On three pieces, Tune-Up, Sandu and Body and Soul, Montgomery plays a tenor guitar.

The repertoire consists of two of Montgomery's own pieces, Movin' Along and So Do It!, and pieces by Miles Davis, Clifford Brown and Sam Jones, alongside the standard Body and Soul. The album was later reissued in the Original Jazz Classics series, with two extra recordings, and is included in the box set The Complete Riverside Recordings. Scott Yanow wrote on AllMusic that Montgomery made many of his best jazz recordings for Riverside, and that this is an often overlooked gem.
werk/wes-montgomery-movin-along.listen: Listen to Body and Soul and notice how Montgomery plays a familiar melody and how he builds his solo.

werk/wes-montgomery-so-much-guitar.text:
Wes Montgomery recorded So Much Guitar! for Riverside Records, where the album was released in 1961. Orrin Keepnews produced the session and Ray Fowler was the engineer. The guitarist played with a rhythm section of pianist Hank Jones, bassist Ron Carter and drummer Lex Humphries, supplemented by Ray Barretto on congas. That last addition gives the record a rhythmic colour of its own.

The programme mixes original work, such as Twisted Blues, with pieces by Duke Ellington, Neal Hefti and Harold Arlen. The eight performances last from just over two to almost eight minutes. Critics later regarded the record as one of the guitarist's best recordings. Scott Yanow called all eight performances memorable in their own way, and PopMatters spoke of one of the most beautiful records you can put in your player.
werk/wes-montgomery-so-much-guitar.listen: Listen to One for My Baby (And One More for the Road), at almost eight minutes the longest track. Notice how the guitar carries the melody and how the band plays calmly around it.

werk/wes-montgomery-the-incredible-jazz-.text:
This 1960 album brought the guitarist Wes Montgomery to the wider public. He recorded it at Reeves Sound Studios in New York, on 26 and 28 January, with producer Orrin Keepnews. Pianist Tommy Flanagan, bassist Percy Heath and drummer Albert Heath accompanied him.

The record shows two hallmarks of his playing: playing with the thumb instead of with a plectrum, and playing in octaves. He combines original tunes such as D-Natural Blues, Four on Six and West Coast Blues with jazz standards such as Sonny Rollins's Airegin and Polka Dots and Moonbeams. Many fans and critics see this as the peak of his studio work. According to AllMusic, the record established him as the most impressive modern guitarist of his time. In 2017 the Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry.
werk/wes-montgomery-the-incredible-jazz-.listen: On Four On Six (Remastered 2025), listen to the guitar lines played in octaves. Notice the warm sound of the thumb.

werk/wham-make-it-big.text:
For their second album, Wham! were given more say over the production, and George Michael was also credited as a producer. Most of it was written and recorded in six weeks, from the beginning of July 1984, at Studio Miraval in the south of France. There Michael could escape the press. Most of the songs were recorded with a real rhythm section. Their first album Fantastic was a hit in England, but had made no impact in America.

Make It Big became a great success and reached number one in both America and England. All four singles reached the top three in both countries. The video for Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go showed the duo in shirts bearing the slogan Choose Life. The video for Freedom was recorded during a concert in China, because Wham! were the first Western pop act to tour there. Rolling Stone called the record an almost flawless pop album. AllMusic later spoke of an exuberant set of new wave pop and soul.
werk/wham-make-it-big.listen: Listen to Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go and notice how lively the rhythm section sounds, with real players instead of just machines.

werk/whitesnake-come-an-get-it.text:
Whitesnake's fourth album was released in 1981 and reached number 2 in Great Britain. Only Kings of the Wild Frontier by Adam and the Ants kept it from the top. The album stayed on the chart for 23 weeks. Don't Break My Heart Again and Would I Lie to You were released as singles, the first reaching the British top 20.

The sleeve is by the British artist Malcolm Horton, after the band had rejected the ideas of the record company EMI. On the front a white snake is trapped in a glass apple; on the back the apple is broken and the snake has escaped: temptation becoming too strong. The snake's tongue caused a stir and was reportedly retouched away in America. The band then toured for five months, including with Judas Priest, and for the first time played Monsters of Rock at Castle Donington.
werk/whitesnake-come-an-get-it.listen: Listen to Don't Break My Heart Again, the single that reached the British top 20, and consider why this song in particular was chosen as the hit.

werk/whitesnake-lovehunter.text:
Whitesnake recorded their second studio album in 1979, at Clearwell Castle, again with producer Martin Birch. It was the last album with drummer Dave Dowle, who was then replaced by Ian Paice, formerly of Deep Purple. With this album the band reached the British top 30 for the first time.

Long Way from Home opens the album and made the British singles chart. Walking in the Shadow of the Blues is regarded as one of the best-loved early songs: David Coverdale and Bernie Marsden came up with the music very quickly, and Coverdale felt that it summed up his musical attitude at the time. The sleeve, by the fantasy artist Chris Achilleos, with a naked woman on a snake, caused a great deal of fuss. In the United States it was partly covered up. The Rolling Stone Album Guide thought the playing was as good as on an early Deep Purple album.
werk/whitesnake-lovehunter.listen: Listen to Walking in the Shadow of the Blues and notice how Coverdale's voice and the guitars alternate in this blues-rock song.

werk/whitesnake-ready-an-willing.text:
Whitesnake's third album was released on 23 May 1980. It was the first with drummer Ian Paice, who had previously played in Deep Purple together with singer David Coverdale and keyboard player Jon Lord. Three former Deep Purple members were thus in one band.

The album contains two British hits: Fool for Your Loving and the title song Ready an' Willing (Sweet Satisfaction). Blindman had already appeared on Coverdale's first solo album White Snake and was re-recorded here. It reached number 6 on the British chart and was the group's first album to chart outside the United Kingdom as well.
werk/whitesnake-ready-an-willing.listen: Listen to Blindman and bear in mind that Coverdale had put this song on his solo album before. Notice what the band version does differently.

werk/whitesnake-trouble.text:
After David Coverdale had left Deep Purple, he formed a band in 1978 to promote his solo work. Whitesnake played their first gig on 3 March 1978. With the EP Snakebite, which reached number 61, they secured a contract with EMI. In July 1978 the band recorded their first proper studio album at Central Recorders in London, with producer Martin Birch. Recording and mixing took only ten days. Micky Moody and Bernie Marsden played guitar and sang backing vocals. Marsden himself sings on Free Flight.

Coverdale wrote most of it, apart from Day Tripper by Lennon and McCartney. Don't Mess With Me is by the whole band. According to him, the title came partly from the fact that his first child was born during the recording. The sleeve shows a snake; in America the album received a different sleeve with a snake coming out of a purple egg cell.
werk/whitesnake-trouble.listen: Listen to Day Tripper and notice what the band does with this song by the Beatles.

werk/whitney-houston-i-m-your-baby-tonig.text:
I'm Your Baby Tonight is Whitney Houston's third album, released on 6 November 1990 by Arista Records. After her poppy second record, Black critics accused her of neglecting her R&B and soul roots. This time she took creative control for the first time and received a credit as executive producer. She brought in the team of L.A. Reid and Babyface, who made the title song, Miracle and My Name Is Not Susan, among others, and she also continued to work with producer Narada Michael Walden.

The sound combines new jack swing with hip hop, funk and dance and sounds more mature than before. The only duet, We Didn't Know, she sang with Stevie Wonder. The title song and All the Man That I Need both reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100. The album reached number three on the American chart and topped the R&B chart. Later it was seen as a turning point in her career.
werk/whitney-houston-i-m-your-baby-tonig.listen: Listen to Feels So Good and notice the relaxed mood, which according to the producer was shaped by the music of Marvin Gaye.

werk/whitney-houston-my-love-is-your-lov.text:
My Love Is Your Love is Whitney Houston's fourth studio album, released on 17 November 1998 by Arista Records. It was her first studio record in eight years. Label boss Clive Davis felt she had been away so long that he wrote her a letter in 1997. At first, material was still being sought for a compilation album, but after It's Not Right but It's Okay by Rodney Jerkins, the project grew into a new studio record. Missy Elliott, Wyclef Jean and Babyface also worked on it.

The album opts for contemporary R&B and hip hop, with funk, reggae and soul as well. The recording took six to seven weeks, the fastest of her career. The duet When You Believe with Mariah Carey won an Oscar, and It's Not Right but It's Okay a Grammy. Critics gave the record some of the best reviews of her career.
werk/whitney-houston-my-love-is-your-lov.listen: Listen to When You Believe and notice how the two voices sing together.

werk/wiley-playtime-is-over.text:
Playtime Is Over is the third studio album by the English grime artist Wiley. It was released on 4 June 2007 on Big Dada Recordings and was recorded in Bow in east London. On the same day Maths + English by Dizzee Rascal, his former protégé, came out. The album reached number 71 on the British album chart. In the week before its release it was the featured album on MySpace.

On the record Wiley tackles his feud with Dizzee Rascal in Letter 2 Dizzee. Dizzee later answered with Pussyole, on his own album. No Qualms uses a sample of Poomplex by Jme from 2006 and is a response to a diss track by Nasty Jack, Pimp on Flows.
werk/wiley-playtime-is-over.listen: Listen to Letter 2 Dizzee: notice how Wiley speaks out about the feud with Dizzee Rascal in the lyrics.

werk/wiley-see-clear-now.text:
See Clear Now is the fifth studio album by the English grime artist Wiley. It was released on 10 November 2008. The release had first been planned for 13 October of that year, under the title I See Clear. Wiley called it his first pop album. He wanted to push boundaries and still stay in the charts with songs that move people.

On the album he works with the electropop group Hot Chip and with DJ and producer Mark Ronson, who can be heard on Cash in My Pocket. The first single was Wearing My Rolex, followed by Summertime and Cash in My Pocket. Wiley himself said that anyone looking for something less commercial would do better to play Race Against Time from 2009, because there he had more artistic control.
werk/wiley-see-clear-now.listen: Listen to Step By Step, on which Hot Chip take part, and notice how a grime rapper moves within a pop-like, electronic sound.

werk/willie-colon-cosa-nuestra.text:
Cosa Nuestra means Our Thing, and that suits an album made by a close-knit team. Willie Colón made the record together with singer Héctor Lavoe. Jerry Masucci, the boss of Fania, was producer, and Johnny Pacheco led the sessions. The band included Milton Cardona on congas, Santi González on bass and José Torres on piano, among others. Izzy Sanabria designed the sleeve, with a photograph by Henri Wolfe.

It was the duo's first record to go gold. La Gran Fuga, El Juicio and Lo Mato followed. In October 2024, Rolling Stone placed the album on its list of the fifty greatest salsa records of all time.
werk/willie-colon-cosa-nuestra.listen: Listen to Che Che Colé and notice how Héctor Lavoe's singing relates to the band beneath it.

werk/willie-colon-el-juicio.text:
El Juicio, which means The Judgment, was released in 1972 on Fania Records. It is the third record by Willie Colón and Héctor Lavoe to go gold, after Cosa Nuestra and La Gran Fuga and before Lo Mato. On this album Colón was not only bandleader but also producer, arranger, composer, trombonist and flautist.

The record has eight tracks, including Timbalero, Aguanile and Pan Y Agua. Lavoe sings and co-wrote. For some tracks, material was drawn from the work of other composers, such as C. Alonso Curet. Johnny Pacheco also took part, as a chorus member and as leader of the sessions. The band included Milton Cardona on congas, Santi González on bass and Joe Torres on piano, among others. The sleeve was designed by Aggie Whelan, under the art direction of Izzy Sanabria.
werk/willie-colon-el-juicio.listen: Listen to Aguanile and notice the percussion, because it gives the song its drive.

werk/willie-colon-the-hustler.text:
The Hustler is the second studio album by Willie Colón and Héctor Lavoe. It was released in 1968 on Fania Records and has seven tracks, from The Hustler itself to Havana, which at almost seven minutes is the longest. The record is the first to contain the song Qué Lío, which the source calls a bolero.

That song would later play an important role in Marc Anthony's album El Cantante and in the film of the same title. The sleeve also has a story. The image of Colón in front of a pool table refers to the 1961 film The Hustler with Paul Newman and Jackie Gleason. The photograph was taken at Ridgewood Grove Billiards in Yonkers, the business of Jerry Masucci's father.
werk/willie-colon-the-hustler.listen: Listen to Qué Lío, which was given new life decades later by Marc Anthony, and notice its calm, bolero-like character.

werk/willie-nelson-and-then-i-wrote.text:
At first Willie Nelson wrote his songs for others. After his own records on D Records came to nothing, he sold songs, and Family Bible became a hit for Claude Gray in 1960. In Nashville he signed as a songwriter with Pamper Music, and Hello Walls, Night Life and Crazy became hits for Faron Young, Ray Price and Patsy Cline. He then signed with Liberty Records.

Producer Joe Allison let him sing in his own way. The recording began in August 1962 in Nashville and was finished in September in Los Angeles, with guitarists such as Billy Strange and Roy Nichols. The debut contains many songs that others had already made famous. The biggest hit was Touch Me, a slow, sad blues with vocal harmonies, which reached number 7 on the Billboard country chart. AllMusic gave the album four out of five stars.
werk/willie-nelson-and-then-i-wrote.listen: Listen to Crazy and notice how his voice gives the rhythm of the melody a loose twist of its own.

werk/willie-nelson-country-willie-his-ow.text:
Liberty released Willie Nelson's first two albums in 1962 and 1963, after country stars such as Faron Young and Patsy Cline had scored hits with his songs. When Liberty closed its country division after the arrival of The Beatles, Chet Atkins signed him to RCA. Country Willie: His Own Songs was his first album for that label.

Atkins and he recorded most of it in January and April 1965. The album contains new versions of his best-known compositions of that time, such as Night Life and Funny How Time Slips Away, alongside newer work such as Healing Hands of Time. One Day at a Time and My Own Peculiar Way offer something of his personal outlook on life. Atkins added heavy strings and choruses, and he later wrote that this did not work. Sales remained small, except in Texas, where the album strengthened his name as a Nashville star.
werk/willie-nelson-country-willie-his-ow.listen: In Night Life, listen to the strings and choruses that Atkins added to the song. Notice how heavy that arrangement is and what it does to the song itself.

werk/willie-nelson-red-headed-stranger.text:
After his years at Atlantic, Willie Nelson signed with Columbia, which gave him complete creative freedom. On the way back from a ski holiday in Colorado to Austin, he conceived a Western story around Tale of the Red Headed Stranger, a song that he had played as a disc jockey. He recorded the album in five days at Autumn Sound Studios in Garland, Texas, for little money. The arrangements remained sparse: guitar, piano by his sister Bobbie, drums, harmonica and mandolin.

It is a concept album about a fugitive who kills his wife and her lover. Original songs sit alongside older numbers such as Blue Eyes Crying In the Rain, which as a single became his first number one. The management of Columbia at first thought they were listening to a demo, but the record became a great success with country and pop listeners. The title became a lasting nickname for the singer.
werk/willie-nelson-red-headed-stranger.listen: Listen to Blue Eyes Crying In the Rain and notice how little is heard: mostly a guitar and a voice, without embellishment.

werk/wim-sonneveld-het-dorp.text: In 1974, Het dorp by the cabaret artist Wim Sonneveld was released, shortly after his death. It is an adaptation of La montagne by the French chansonnier Jean Ferrat. The Dutch text is by Friso Wiegersma. The song is about a village that has been made unrecognisable by progress. The Dutch-language songs of those years came more from Paris than from Liverpool. Het dorp has ranked high in the Top 2000 for years.
werk/wim-sonneveld-het-dorp.listen: Hear how Sonneveld tells the song more than he sings it, like a chansonnier, with nostalgia for a vanished world.

werk/within-temptation-enter.text:
Within Temptation made Enter as their debut album for the label DSFA Records. A week after the contract was signed, recording began at Studio Moskou in Utrecht, with producer Lex Vogelaar of the death metal band Orphanage. The album consisted of new versions of demos and had to be finished within three weeks. Singer Sharon den Adel had a day and a half for her parts. There was little time to let the songs grow.

The sound lies between gothic metal and doom, with long instrumental passages and few lyrics. Besides Sharon den Adel's singing, you hear the raw grunts of guitarist Robert Westerholt, something the band later hardly ever did again. The lyrics deal with darkness, ghosts and war. Restless was the only single. On release the album failed to make the Dutch chart, but in 2002 it reached number 32 after all, following the success of Ice Queen.
werk/within-temptation-enter.listen: In Deep Within, listen to the contrast between Sharon den Adel's singing and the grunts: the heavy voice comes from guest vocalist George Oosthoek.

werk/within-temptation-ice-queen.text: In January 2002, Ice Queen by Within Temptation from Waddinxveen became a big hit. This happened because fans massively requested the video on the music channel The Box. The band makes symphonic metal: heavy guitars combined with orchestral sounds and the clear voice of Sharon den Adel. Within Temptation became popular above all in Germany and beyond, and is among the most successful bands in the genre.
werk/within-temptation-ice-queen.listen: Hear the contrast between the heavy guitars and Sharon den Adel's light, almost classical singing voice.

werk/within-temptation-the-heart-of-ever.text:
The Heart of Everything is the fourth album by the Dutch symphonic metal band Within Temptation. Composing began at the end of 2005 and the recording took half a year in 2006. The album was released on 12 March 2007 in Europe on GUN Records and later that year in North America on Roadrunner Records. The band drew inspiration from books and from personal moments, above all the making of choices. That is why Lady Justice appears on the cover, a design by the Dutch artist Erwin Olaf.

Singer Sharon den Adel sees it as the record on which the band finally achieved the symphonic sound. Our Solemn Hour is about people being sacrificed in wars while we learn nothing from them. Frozen is about child abuse, and the proceeds from that single went to Child Helpline International. What Have You Done was the first and most successful single. The album reached number one in the Netherlands and received positive reviews.
werk/within-temptation-the-heart-of-ever.listen: Listen to Frozen, a song about child abuse, and notice how the band translates a heavy subject into symphonic metal.

werk/wizkid-made-in-lagos.text:
Wizkid's fourth studio album was released on 30 October 2020. It followed Sounds from the Other Side from 2017, with stand-alone singles and the EP Soundman Vol. 1, a test for the Afro-European market, in between. The release was pushed back a few weeks because of the End SARS protests in Nigeria. P2J was executive producer, and guests such as Burna Boy, Skepta, H.E.R. and Tems sing along.

The music mixes Afrobeats and R&B, with a mid-tempo production and Auto-Tuned melodies. Local African percussion forms the core of the beats. Smile with H.E.R. was the first single. Essence with Tems became the biggest success: the remix with Justin Bieber was the highest-charting single by an African act on the Billboard Hot 100. Critics praised the cohesion and the rich production. The album received a Grammy nomination for Best Global Music Album.
werk/wizkid-made-in-lagos.listen: In Essence, listen to the way Tems's vocals and the lead vocals alternate over a calm, mid-tempo rhythm. Notice how the percussion carries the song without dominating.

werk/wolf-biermann-chausseestra-e-131.text:
Chausseestraße 131 was the second LP by the East German singer-songwriter and poet Wolf Biermann, after Wolf Biermann (Ost) zu Gast bei Wolfgang Neuss (West), which he made together with Wolfgang Neuss. It was his first album after the SED had banned him from performing or releasing music through the state company VEB Deutsche Schallplatten. A professional studio was therefore out of reach. Biermann recorded the record in his own apartment, at the address in the title, with a Grundig tape recorder and a Sennheiser microphone that had been smuggled in from West Germany. On the recording you therefore hear the traffic outside.

In 1969 Biermann received the Fontane Prize. He publicly passed it on to the APO, the protest movement of German students, and donated 10,000 marks to the lawyer Horst Mahler.
werk/wolf-biermann-chausseestra-e-131.listen: Listen to Das Barlach-Lied and notice how bare the recording sounds, as if you were sitting in the room itself. Can you also hear sounds from outside?

werk/wynton-marsalis-black-codes-from-th.text:
Black Codes (From the Underground) was released in 1985. Wynton Marsalis played trumpet in a quintet with his brother Branford on tenor and soprano saxophone, Kenny Kirkland on piano, Charnett Moffett on double bass and Jeff Watts on drums. On Aural Oasis, Ron Carter played bass. The producer was Steven Epstein, and the liner notes were written by Stanley Crouch.

The album won two Grammys in 1986. In 2023 the Library of Congress added it to the National Recording Registry. It described it as one of the trumpeter's most beloved and artistically successful recordings: a record that looks back at the acoustic jazz of the mid-twentieth century, but with a touch of its own from the 1980s.
werk/wynton-marsalis-black-codes-from-th.listen: Listen to Black Codes and notice how the trumpet and the saxophone play together with the rhythm section. Try to hear what sounds like acoustic jazz from the mid-twentieth century.

werk/wynton-marsalis-blood-on-the-fields.text:
Blood on the Fields is a jazz oratorio lasting two and a half hours, composed by Wynton Marsalis for the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra. Lincoln Center commissioned it. The work premiered on 28 January 1997 in Woolsey Hall at Yale University and was released the same year on Columbia Records. It deals with the history of slavery and its aftermath in the United States.

It tells the story of two slaves, Jesse and Leona, on their difficult road to freedom. The story shows that the freedom of the individual is inseparably linked to the liberation of the community and of the whole country. Miles Griffith sings Jesse, Cassandra Wilson sings Leona and Jon Hendricks plays the wise man. In 1997 the oratorio won the Pulitzer Prize for Music, the first time the prize was awarded for a jazz composition. Previously it had been reserved for classical composers.
werk/wynton-marsalis-blood-on-the-fields.listen: Listen to the opening track Calling the Indians Out and bear in mind that this is the beginning of a two-and-a-half-hour story told in jazz.

werk/wynton-marsalis-trumpet-concertos.text:
On this album Wynton Marsalis plays trumpet concertos by Joseph Haydn, Leopold Mozart and Johann Nepomuk Hummel. He was accompanied by the National Philharmonic Orchestra under Raymond Leppard. Thomas Mowrey produced the record. It was his first classical album and it came out at the same time as his second jazz album, Think of One. Thus the twenty-one-year-old Marsalis was, according to AllMusic, the most celebrated interpreter of both classical music and jazz since Benny Goodman.

Marsalis wrote the cadenza in the first movement of the Haydn concerto himself. It begins with two musical questions, which he answers boldly, followed by dialogues and large leaps, all within the classical style. Gramophone magazine called his playing very impressive. In 1984 the album won a Grammy Award for Best Instrumental Soloist with Orchestra.
werk/wynton-marsalis-trumpet-concertos.listen: Listen to the first movement of the concerto in E-flat and notice the cadenza, in which the trumpet seems to ask questions and answer them itself.

werk/yann-tiersen-good-bye-lenin.text:
This album is the soundtrack of the 2003 film Good Bye, Lenin!, starring Daniel Brühl and Katrin Sass. Almost all the music was written by Yann Tiersen. The only exception is the sung version of Summer 78, sung by Claire Pichet.

The music recalls Tiersen's best-known film work, the soundtrack of Amélie, which was strongly influenced by French music. A piece from Amélie, Comptine d'un autre été : L'après-midi, is heard in the film during the family's first outing to West Berlin, but is not on this record. In some regions the album was released with Copy Control, a copy protection.
werk/yann-tiersen-good-bye-lenin.listen: Listen to Summer 78 (1) and notice which instruments carry the melody and how simple the theme is.

werk/yann-tiersen-les-retrouvailles.text:
Les Retrouvailles is the fifth studio album by the French musician Yann Tiersen and was released in 2005 on the label Ici, d'ailleurs. As on all his records he shows his versatility: he plays accordion, piano, mandolin and harpsichord, among other instruments, but toy piano, vibraphone and ondes Martenot can also be heard. The Orchestre National de Paris plays on five tracks.

New is the number of guest singers, French and English-language. Elizabeth Fraser of the Cocteau Twins sings in Kala and Mary, Jane Birkin in Plus d'hiver and Stuart Staples of the Tindersticks in A Secret Place. Miossec and Dominique A sing together in Le Jour de l'ouverture. The album comes with a DVD containing a short film, La Traversée, which shows the making of the record and also includes live versions of some of the tracks.
werk/yann-tiersen-les-retrouvailles.listen: Listen to Kala and notice how Elizabeth Fraser's voice relates to the orchestra and the cello.

werk/yasunori-mitsuda-kirite.text:
Kirite is a 2005 album by the composer Yasunori Mitsuda, based on The Five Seasons of Kirite, a story by Masato Kato. Mitsuda and Kato had previously collaborated on Chrono Trigger, Xenogears and Chrono Cross. This time it was not made into a computer game. They conceived the concept in 2003. The album was released together with Kato's story in Japanese and a collection of nature photographs.

The story is set in a world of magic and fantasy, where a boy, a girl and a darkness meet and the world quietly begins to go mad. The music contains influences from Celtic music, jazz and ambient sound. Besides piano and vocals, violin, bouzouki, tin whistle, shinobue and shakuhachi are heard, among others.
werk/yasunori-mitsuda-kirite.listen: Listen to The Forest of Lapis Lazuli and try to hear which instruments give the Celtic colour and which the Japanese.

werk/yellow-magic-orchestra-solid-state-.text:
For the Japanese group's second album, music from earlier work came together. Behind the Mask had already been made in 1978 for a Seiko commercial, with synthesizers for the melody and digital gated reverb on the snare drum. Later covers came from Michael Jackson and Eric Clapton, among others.

The 1979 album is regarded as an early example of synth-pop and contributed to the development of techno. Technopolis, a tribute to Tokyo as an electronic centre, already used the term techno in its title. Rydeen later received a chiptune arrangement for an arcade game. The title track is new wave-style synth rock, and there is also an adaptation of the Beatles' Day Tripper. It was the group's most successful album in Japan. It won the Best Album Award at the Japan Record Awards and sold two million copies.
werk/yellow-magic-orchestra-solid-state-.listen: Listen to Technopolis, a tribute to Tokyo as the electronic capital. Which electronic sounds carry the melody here?

werk/yellowman-mister-yellowman.text:
Mister Yellowman is the first studio album by the Jamaican deejay Yellowman. In October 1982 it was released on Greensleeves in England, and under the title Duppy or Gunman in Jamaica. It was his first record with producer Henry Junjo Lawes. The Roots Radics and Earl Chinna Smith's Hi Times band played, and Lawes made a warm mixture of dancehall rhythms and dub out of it.

Billboard wrote that reggae is stripped down to the minimum here, with vocals that are almost as often rapped as sung. Allmusic called it a masterly deejay record. Trouser Press praised Mister Chin, Two to Six Super Mix and Yellowman Getting Married, which was inspired by My Fair Lady. Mojo and Pitchfork later included the record in their lists.
werk/yellowman-mister-yellowman.listen: Listen to Yellowman Getting Married and notice how he talks and sings at the same time.

werk/yes-close-to-the-edge.text:
After the success of Fragile, Yes began rehearsing in May 1972 in a dance hall in Shepherd's Bush. Jon Anderson and Steve Howe had collected sketches along the way, but not a single song was finished. The group put those fragments together in the studio step by step. Producer and engineer Eddy Offord built a wooden stage at Advision Studios in London so that the band would sound livelier. The recording was so gruelling that drummer Bill Bruford left for King Crimson.

The album consists of just three long pieces. Close to the Edge, 18 minutes, is a suite in four parts with themes from Hermann Hesse's Siddhartha. And You and I is pastoral and folk-like, while Siberian Khatru is a hard-driving rocker. Rick Wakeman used Mellotron and church organ. Roger Dean's green-coloured sleeve also introduced the group's well-known logo. The record was a great success, reaching number 3 on the American Billboard 200.
werk/yes-close-to-the-edge.listen: Listen to And You and I and notice the contrast with the rest of the record: acoustic guitar and calm vocals, before the music grows bigger.

werk/yes-relayer.text:
Relayer was made after keyboard player Rick Wakeman had left Yes, because he did not like the direction of Tales From Topographic Oceans. The band rehearsed as a quartet and recorded in the studio that bassist Chris Squire had at his home in Virginia Water. After auditions with Vangelis, among others, the choice fell on the Swiss Patrick Moraz, and this is the only studio record on which he plays. The production was in the hands of the band and Eddy Offord.

The sound is fiercer, with influences from jazz fusion and funk. The record has three tracks: The Gates of Delirium, inspired by Tolstoy's War and Peace, with a battle that ends in a soft prayer, and Sound Chaser and To Be Over. The album reached number four in England.
werk/yes-relayer.listen: Listen to The Gates of Delirium and notice how the battle turns into the calm ending.

werk/yes-tales-from-topographic-oceans.text:
Singer Jon Anderson got the idea for Tales From Topographic Oceans in a hotel room in Tokyo, after reading in Autobiography of a Yogi about four categories of Hindu texts. Together with guitarist Steve Howe he worked it out. After weeks of rehearsal, Yes decided to make a double album with four tracks of between 18 and 21 minutes each. It was the first album with drummer Alan White. Keyboard player Rick Wakeman was critical of the concept. At Morgan Studios in London, the studio was set up as a farm.

The album spent two weeks at number one in England. The critical response was sharply divided: some saw it as a symbol of the excess of progressive rock, and later the reviews became milder.
werk/yes-tales-from-topographic-oceans.listen: Listen to The Revealing Science of God and follow how a piece of this length builds up in sections.

werk/yes-time-and-a-word.text:
Yes's second album came about in a short time. After the 1969 debut, the group kept touring intensively and recorded in the breaks at Advision Studios in London, with producer Tony Colton and engineer Eddy Offord. For the first time a small orchestra played along: a brass section of session musicians and strings from the Royal College of Music, with arrangements by Tony Cox. Guitarist Peter Banks thought little of it, tension rose, and in 1970 Steve Howe took his place.

Singer Jon Anderson wrote lyrics that shifted from simple love themes to larger subjects. The opener No Opportunity Necessary, No Experience Needed is a song by Richie Havens and begins with an orchestral theme from the film The Big Country. The Prophet borrows a theme from Jupiter by Gustav Holst. The reviews were mixed, but the album became the group's first to reach the British album chart, at number 45.
werk/yes-time-and-a-word.listen: In The Prophet, listen to the theme borrowed from Jupiter by Gustav Holst: do you recognise it, and how does it sound within a rock song with orchestra?

werk/yes-yes.text:
Yes is the debut album by the band Yes, released in England on 25 July 1969 by Atlantic. The group had been formed in the summer of 1968 with Jon Anderson, Chris Squire, Peter Banks, Bill Bruford and Tony Kaye, toured around England and signed with Atlantic in March 1969. The recording took place in the spring of 1969 at Advision and Trident Studios in London, with producer Paul Clay.

The album contains covers of Every Little Thing by the Beatles and I See You by the Byrds. Beyond and Before, written by Squire and Clive Bailey, opened the live shows and contains three-part harmonies that quickly became a trademark. Critics were positive, but the album did not reach the charts in either country.
werk/yes-yes.listen: In Beyond and Before, listen to the three-part harmonies, which quickly became a trademark of the band.

werk/yo-yo-ma-hush.text:
Hush is a collaboration between cellist Yo-Yo Ma and singer Bobby McFerrin, released on the label Sony Masterworks. The two met in 1988 at a celebration for Leonard Bernstein. McFerrin and Steven Epstein produced the album. McFerrin wrote five tracks and together they arranged three compositions by Johann Sebastian Bach. According to McFerrin, the cellist hesitated to improvise during the recording.

The programme mixes classical, folk and original work: Vivaldi, Rachmaninov, Gounod and Rimsky-Korsakov, the children's song Hush Little Baby and McFerrin's own pieces. One newspaper heard in his compositions mainly New Age with cleverly layered overdubs, apart from Hoedown!, which contains many country fiddle licks. Another newspaper praised Stars as the best track. The Washington Post appreciated the combination of the expressive cellist with the humour, playfulness and musicality of the singer. The record reached number 93 on the Billboard 200.
werk/yo-yo-ma-hush.listen: On Stars, listen to the singer's melody and how the cello complements it, and notice how voice and cello together form one sound.

werk/yoko-ono-approximately-infinite-uni.text:
This double album from early 1973 is Yoko Ono's third solo album and was released on Apple Records. After two experimental avant-garde records, she opted for a more conventional pop and rock sound, with feminist rock here and there. The recording took place at The Record Plant in New York. Ono produced together with John Lennon, for whom this was a rare musical activity after the failure of Some Time in New York City.

The New York band Elephant's Memory played along. Lennon sang the last verse of I Want My Love to Rest Tonight and played guitar under the pseudonym Joel Nohnn. Mick Jagger dropped in during some of the sessions. The gatefold sleeve contains the essay The Feminization of Society. The album reached number 193 in the United States.
werk/yoko-ono-approximately-infinite-uni.listen: Listen to Is Winter Here to Stay? and notice Mick Jagger's guitar.
